scope: Current research queue only. This is a qualitative, preregistration-style plan, not validation, a score projection, a submission artifact, or permission to bypass protocol_preflight.require_feasible(). The older registry/h86c_hypotheses.json is preserved as the original preregistration snapshot, not the current status register.

current_protocol_status.implication: Every nonempty candidate violates the literal overlap gate. No top hypothesis can be built or tested until the protocol contradiction is resolved by an authorized upstream change; no threshold or exception is introduced here.

ranking_basis: Qualitative expected information gain for fault-displacement detection, relevance to the unmapped-fault target, competition-band self-sufficiency, reviewed-method novelty, source readiness, and implementation cost. This is a low-confidence research ordering, not a numerical DTI prediction or claim of leaderboard improvement. The standalone SPBT negative control lowers the prior for its separate Laplace-curvature extension; the extension remains untested.
evidence_boundary: All current candidates have holdout_dti=null and ci95=null. Historical numbers appear only under previously_tested_methods and retain their evaluator, withheld-positive count, and 95% CI. Withheld known-catalogue segments are a proxy, not direct proof of recovery of genuinely uncatalogued expert faults. No fault detector establishes a geothermal vent, heat source, permeability, fluid saturation, or commercial resource.

hypotheses.name: Cross-corridor GeoDAWN magnetic-marker translation with radiometric contact control
layers: competition tmi_hg (Band 3) and tmi_vg (Band 9), combined as analytical magnetic tilt theta_mag = atan2(tmi_vg, tmi_hg)
competition tc (Band 6), pixel-verified as radiometric Total Count and used only as a surficial-contact control, not magnetic tilt
hypotheses.signature: Test label-free, strike-windowed phase correlation of RTP and analytical magnetic-tilt marker profiles on opposite sides of candidate corridors. Require a consistent, nonzero lateral translation across adjacent strike windows, matched marker polarity/shape, and continuity through the corridor; compare against zero-shift and phase-scrambled controls. Use Band 6 Total Count only to flag radiometric/alluvial boundaries without a matching magnetic-marker offset. Estimate survey-seam directions from acquisition metadata rather than assuming a fixed azimuth. The magnetic products share acquisition/source ancestry and are not independent measurements.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: A blind transfer or accommodation fault may translate a buried volcanic marker beneath basin fill without producing a strong surface scarp. This is a mechanism to test, not an assertion that a detected magnetic offset is a fault or that a withheld catalogue segment represents a genuinely uncatalogued fault.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: The reviewed GEMSDOE86 lanes principally score ridges, gradients, contacts, or local structural attributes; this hypothesis tests two-sided cross-corridor translation rather than a pointwise edge. The reviewed sibling metadata did not identify this exact phase-lag mechanism, but that search is not proof of global or competition-wide originality. The current shared feature cache and required raw feature TIFF are absent locally.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Intrusive contacts, primary volcanic-flow terminations, remanent-polarity changes, and GeoDAWN flight-line/tie-line leveling seams.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Highest qualitative opportunity in this untested queue, with low confidence: displacement is more directly aligned to fault-trace prediction than a generic edge. No numeric HOLDOUT-DTI or leaderboard improvement is forecast.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high; phase-correlation windows, acquisition-seam controls, matched controls, cache identity checks, and buffered whole-segment holdout. Runtime is unbenchmarked.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_VIABLE_NOW: the official GeoDAWN release is documented, but data/training_features.tif and the actual shared feature cache are absent in this checkout; the protocol preflight blocks construction before any feature is built.
hypotheses.obtainability: Competition-native bands avoid a new external product, but the actual local feature stack/cache must be restored from its authorized, hash-pinned source before execution. A raw owner mirror is not the shared cache and is not organizer-authenticated.
planned_controls: matched fold-fair baseline on the identical withheld fault segments

hypotheses.name: Signed paired-throw basement/gravity concordance augmented with Laplace gravity curvature
hypotheses.signature: Retain the signed cross-flank basement/gravity throw test, then add the footprint-masked, spatially regularized Laplace vertical gravity-curvature dipole g_zz = -(d_x Band18 - d_y Band11) as an additional geometric constraint along the same strike-consistent corridor. Compare with the standalone SPBT baseline and a polarity-scrambled control. Mask nodata before derivatives and do not treat Band 13, Bands 11/18, or their derived curvature as independent observations: they share gravity-data ancestry. The archived standalone SPBT implementation did not include this Laplace term.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Hypothesis: alluvial/playa burial may mute surface slope while a blind intrabasin growth fault retains basement-depth and gravity flank structure; the curvature term could sharpen the cross-strike dipole geometry. Whole-segment holdout must test this before any claim about unmapped faults.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: The standalone signed basement/gravity SPBT was already tested in H86E E1-E2 and falsified against its recorded polarity-scrambled and spaced-random controls. This is not a claim of a new standalone SPBT. The distinct proposed extension adds regularized Laplace gravity curvature; H86E E1-E2 did not implement or test that term. No reviewed GEMSDOE86 lane implemented this exact extension, but its incremental value over the negative base remains unknown.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Unfaulted paleovalley margins, buried caldera-moat density boundaries, gravity-inversion artifacts, and spatially correlated gravity-resampling noise.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Low-to-moderate qualitative opportunity, ranked below MMT because the standalone base was negative and the added curvature is derived from the same gravity field. It remains a falsifiable, untested extension; no numeric gain is forecast.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high; exact band masking, derivative regularization/sensitivity analysis, comparison against the negative base and polarity control, then buffered spatial holdout. Runtime is unbenchmarked.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_VIABLE_NOW: the necessary competition feature stack is absent locally, and protocol_preflight blocks feature construction. The prior physics receipt verifies band semantics, not present byte availability.
hypotheses.obtainability: Uses competition-native gravity and terrain bands, but the actual local feature stack/shared cache must be restored and hash-bound before execution. The Laplace extension has not been run or validated.
planned_controls: previously tested standalone SPBT baseline, rerun only if authorized under the same folds
identical buffered whole-segment holdout and paired confidence interval

hypotheses.name: Hydrothermal magnetite-destruction troughs aligned with paleo-sinter and shallow thermal anomalies
layers: competition rtp (Band 2), tmi_vg (Band 9), cond_surf (Band 17), geod_shearrate (Band 7), geod_dilaterate (Band 8), and tc (Band 6, radiometric Total Count)
hypotheses.signature: Seek strike-continuous RTP troughs with positive cross-strike trough curvature and flanking shoulders, co-located with shallow conductivity and spatially aligned paleo-sinter/thermal anomalies in dilatant corridors. Compare against phase-scrambled and point-location controls; run a single-feature leakage canary for each external layer. A magnetic trough or geothermal deposit alone is not diagnostic of a fault.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Concealed permeable structures could focus hydrothermal alteration and surface/near-surface thermal manifestations even where a fault scarp is buried or absent. The benchmark target is fault traces, not geothermal deposits, so vent/sinter association must be tested rather than assumed.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: H86D-CTHB used positive magnetic-ridge and radial point-halo features. This proposal tests the sign-reversed trough/shoulder geometry plus pairwise spatial alignment, not a generic deposit halo. It excludes fault-compilation polygons and every distance-to-known-fault field. The screened local novelty review is limited to the cited repository/fleet scope.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Primary low-susceptibility felsic tuff, remanent-polarity volcanic flows, saline playa conductivity, and survey-line artifacts.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Moderate qualitative opportunity but low confidence: the physical association is relevant to concealed hydrothermal conduits, yet geothermal points are not fault labels and may be spatially biased. No numeric gain is forecast.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high; licensed point cleaning, coordinate/grid checks, aligned-corridor construction, point-location controls, leakage canaries, and buffered holdout. Runtime is unbenchmarked.
hypotheses.free_official_source_needed: DOE GDR 1391, CC BY 4.0; source and mirror metadata only, raw bytes not restored
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_VIABLE_NOW: the official GDR listing was previously retrieved and pinned GitHub mirror entries are metadata-reachable, but no raw archive bytes are present locally or hash-verified in this continuation; protocol_preflight also blocks execution.
hypotheses.obtainability: Official DOE GDR 1391 resource page and CC BY 4.0 terms are recorded. GitHub API metadata lists the two pinned mirror archives at their expected sizes, but the expected SHA-256 values are manifest entries, not measurements of local bytes. Restore only through the pinned, licensed source and verify hashes before any use.
planned_controls: per-layer canary; AUC above 0.90 is treated as leakage and stops the run

hypotheses.name: Multi-depth magnetotelluric conductance and conductive heat-flow contrasts
layers: official USGS Great Basin MT conductance product (DOI 10.5066/P9TWT2LU; depth intervals and native resolution not verified)
official USGS conductive heat-flow product (DOI 10.5066/P9BZPVUC; native resolution not verified)
competition cond_surf (Band 17), geod_dilaterate (Band 8), geod_shearrate (Band 7), tmi_hg (Band 3), and tmi_vg (Band 9)
hypotheses.signature: If the official products have adequate coverage and resolution, contrast deeper versus shallow conductance with heat-flow anomalies and positive dilatation; use competition-native magnetic structure only as a coarse spatial constraint. First verify product metadata and the native pixel size; do not downsample a regional proxy and claim 100 m fault localization.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: A deep conductive/thermal corridor could indicate concealed fluid pathways where surficial scarps and single-depth surface conductivity fail to resolve the structure. This is conditional on the source grids resolving relevant scales.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: The competition cond_surf (Band 17) layer is a surface-conductivity proxy, but the reviewed local lanes do not combine verified multi-depth MT conductance and conductive heat-flow grids. This statement is bounded to the reviewed checkout; no outside originality claim is made.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Graphitic or sulfidic stratiform units, saline basin brines, and non-tectonic conductive lithologic contrasts.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Potentially moderate if data resolution matches the fault scale, but presently unrankable scientifically because the relevant binary data, depth bins, and grid resolution are unverified. No numeric gain is forecast.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High; source retrieval, license/coverage audit, reprojection, multiscale resolution tests, leakage canaries, and buffered holdout. Runtime is unbenchmarked.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_VIABLE_YET: official DOI links are identified in the UNR/INGENIOUS page, but no raw grids or verified metadata are available in this checkout; protocol_preflight also blocks execution.
hypotheses.obtainability: Not confirmed. The official DOI records must be accessed and their binary products, license, coverage, depth intervals, and spatial resolution verified and SHA-pinned before this idea can be called viable.
planned_controls: single-feature canary for each imported grid
identical buffered whole-segment holdout with paired interval

hypotheses.name: Cross-watershed persistence of native 1 m 3DEP micro-scarps
layers: official USGS 3DEP native 1 m bare-earth DEM tiles linked by the competition 1m_DEM_links.csv (the CSV and native tiles are absent locally)
competition det_elev (Band 12) and det_elev_slope (Band 19) as lower-resolution controls
hypotheses.signature: Search for signed 5–25 m cross-strike terrain steps that persist across at least three independent drainage divides at native 1 m resolution; veto channels, constant-elevation shorelines, terrace risers, and roads. Validate the source mosaic and tile seams before deriving features.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: A low-slip surface scarp might be smoothed in a 100 m terrain product but persist across catchments in native lidar. This only addresses surface-expressed faults; buried blind faults remain outside this mechanism.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Reviewed local lanes primarily use 100 m competition bands or pre-derived terrain summaries. A pinned owner-mirror entry for lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif is a derived product, not native 1 m tile data and not proof that raw tiles are available.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan shoreline benches, fluvial terrace risers, channel margins, and road/rail embankments.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Moderate qualitative opportunity for surface-rupturing faults only, with low confidence and high cost. No numeric gain is forecast; no conclusion applies to blind structures.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High; tile inventory, native-resolution terrain processing, seam checks, multiple-divide persistence, and holdout evaluation. Runtime is unbenchmarked.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_VIABLE_YET: neither the competition tile-link CSV nor the native 1 m DEM tiles are present. A derived owner-mirror feature is not a substitute. Protocol preflight also blocks execution.
hypotheses.obtainability: The official USGS 3DEP source is identified, but native coverage and tile availability for the competition footprint have not been verified. The linked mirror metadata checked here describes a derived feature product only; no raw tile bytes were downloaded.

required_validation_after_blockers_are_r: Obtain an explicit authorized protocol resolution for the full-support witness contradiction. Do not alter the 0.70 overlap limit, remove witnesses, exempt surfaces, build a candidate surface, or place dots while the current preflight stops.

Restore the actual hash-pinned shared feature cache and all required source bytes; verify licenses, checksums, coverage, band indices in src/gems86/io.py, grid alignment, nodata, and visible-only provenance. Do not substitute a raw mirrored feature TIFF for the shared cache.

Use H86E-MMT as the highest-priority untested lane only after the above blockers clear. Hide complete mapped-fault segments with the prescribed buffer, remove every hidden-segment-derived catalogue feature, and evaluate with the shared gems57-pooled-hide-v2 evaluator against fold-matched controls.
Run a single-feature leakage canary before combinations; AUC greater than 0.90 is leakage and stops the run. Use zero-shift, phase-scrambled, and matched-baseline controls for MMT.

Measure pre-placement surface similarity and the final-dot registry. Stop on rank correlation above 0.90 or more than 70 percent of new dots within 3 px of a prior. A failed/partial scan never establishes uniqueness.

For any authorized experiment, record one JSON run card with method, mimic, HOLDOUT-DTI evaluator, withheld positives, 95 percent CI, registry result, raster SHA, validator, submission name/note, and negative/promote verdict. Stop at three experiments or two hours, whichever comes first; promotion and any weekly slot remain a separate human selector decision.
